jurisdiction.name: Peru
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Peru has a framework AI law (Law 31814 of 2023) and a binding, risk-based regulation under it (Supreme Decree 115-2025-PCM), led by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers' Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation, which also publishes a catalogue of AI applications used by the state. Peru adopted its first National AI Strategy 2026-2030 in May 2026. Law 32314 of 2025 makes the use of AI an aggravating circumstance and adds deepfake offences to the Criminal Code, and Law 32615 of 2026 provides for AI to protect the vicuña. The data protection law and its 2024 regulation set rules on automated decisions, the banking supervisor (SBS) has model-risk rules with AI-specific requirements, and the quality institute INACAL has adopted ISO/IEC 42001 and 23894 as national standards. More than 50 AI bills are before Congress.
lead_institutions: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros - Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital
Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP (SBS)
Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering El Peruano back to 2023, Congress's bill tracker, the digital government secretariat, each ministry and each sector regulator. The national legal database's own search and several regulators' and ministries' websites were not browsed directly. The AI Officer directive was published on 21 October 2026; the AI ethics guidelines required by the AI regulation are not yet published. Institutional AI policies (health ministry, tax authority, competition authority) and pending AI bills are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Approved by Resolución Ministerial N.° 152-2026-PCM dated 29 April 2026 and published in El Peruano on 1 May 2026. The RM makes the ENIA applicable to public administration entities and state companies (private actors may use it as reference) and requires each entity to approve an AI Action Plan of at least three years. Peru's first adopted AI strategy: the 2021-2025 draft strategy was never formally approved (stated in ENIA section 1.3). Record title corrected from the gob.pe page title.
instruments.summary: Peru's first formally adopted national AI strategy, prepared by the PCM-SGTD under the AI Law Regulation, with the objective of developing and strengthening AI governance and management nationwide for inclusive, safe and ethical use. It is organised in four strategic axes (AI talent and capabilities; AI-based innovation and entrepreneurship; ethical and regulatory framework, including mandatory NTP-ISO/IEC 42001 and guidelines on algorithmic transparency and impact assessment; citizen participation and collaboration), with roles for AI governance, a roadmap, resource allocation and monitoring. The approving resolution binds public entities to align their plans with it and adopt institutional AI Action Plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; sets public-sector AI governance roles and action plans.

instruments.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Supreme Decree, countersigned by the President of the Council of Ministers and the Ministers of Education, Production and Justice and Human Rights)
instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 9 September 2025. The decree enters into force 90 business days after publication (the 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th final provisions apply from the day after publication); no calendar effective date is stated. Obligations phase in by entity type (public sector 1-3 years) and, for private developers/implementers, by sector (1 year for health, education, justice, security, economy and finance; up to 4 years for other uses). Earlier id held an explanatory gob.pe page ('Conoce el Reglamento...'); re-pointed to the decree itself. The draft was pre-published by RM 132-2024-PCM.
instruments.summary: Regulation of Law 31814 (36 articles, six titles) setting Peru's risk-based AI regime: it classifies uses as prohibited ('uso indebido') or high-risk (e.g. health, education, justice, finance, access to basic services, hiring), requires algorithmic transparency, human oversight, privacy by design, security measures and a high-risk impact assessment, and sets general obligations for public entities (institutional AI policy, mandatory NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025, AI in digital-government plans) and for private developers and implementers (records, internal policies, training). It establishes the PCM-SGTD governance framework, an AI controlled-testing sandbox, the gob.pe/iaperu channel, a duty on PCM to approve a National AI Strategy within one year, and a complaints route for people harmed by AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Core binding AI rules: risk classification, prohibitions, high-risk obligations, sandbox, mandatory ISO/IEC 42001 adoption.

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 5 July 2023 (approved by Congress 13 June 2023, promulgated 4 July 2023). instruments.summary: Peru's framework AI law: it declares AI promotion of national interest, sets principles for AI development and use (risk-based security standards, multi-stakeholder participation, internet governance, digital society, ethical development, privacy) and defines AI, AI-based systems, emerging technologies and algorithms. It designates the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation, as the national technical-normative authority that directs, evaluates and supervises AI use, and requires it to report annually to Congress on the National Digital Transformation Policy and the National AI Strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding AI law; designates the national AI authority (PCM-SGTD).

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 29 April 2025 (approved by Congress 22 April 2025, promulgated 28 April 2025). In force.
instruments.summary: Amends the Criminal Code (Legislative Decree 635) and the Computer Crimes Law (Law 30096) to make the use, or misuse, of artificial intelligence or analogous technologies a general aggravating circumstance (art. 46). It expressly covers AI-generated content and deepfakes in child sexual abuse material (art. 129-M) and defamation (art. 132), adds aggravated fraud through AI manipulation of a third party's voice, image or movement (art. 196-A), and extends intellectual-property offences and the computer-crimes aggravation to AI use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminal-law provisions specific to AI and deepfakes.

instruments.issuing_authority: Congress of the Republic of Peru
instruments.current_status: Dated 3 July 2011 on the Congress norm page on gob.pe (the law text is dated 'Dado en ... 2 de julio de 2011'). In force; its current Regulation is DS 016-2024-JUS (in force 31 March 2025), which replaced DS 003-2013-JUS.
instruments.summary: Peru's general data protection law, guaranteeing the constitutional right to personal data protection and setting principles, legal bases, data-subject rights, cross-border transfer rules and sanctions, supervised by the National Authority for Personal Data Protection (Ministry of Justice and Human Rights). Article 23 gives data subjects a right to 'objective treatment': not to be subject to a decision with legal or significant effects based solely on processing intended to evaluate aspects of their personality or conduct, which governs automated decision-making by AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law governing AI training and automated decision-making (art. 23).

instruments.summary: New Regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law (135 articles), repealing the 2013 regulation. Relevant to AI, it defines profiling as automated processing, requires information on the existence of automated decisions including profiling, and article 87 details the right not to be subject to decisions, automated or not, with legal or significant effects based solely on automated evaluation without human intervention, with a duty to inform the data subject; it also introduces impact assessments, data protection officers and breach notification.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Implements automated-decision and profiling safeguards applicable to AI systems.

instruments.english_title: SBS Resolution No. 00053-2023: Model Risk Management Regulation
instruments.issuing_authority: Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and Private Pension Fund Administrators (SBS)
instruments.current_status: Resolution dated 6 January 2023 (Lima) and published in El Peruano on 11 January 2023; in force the day after publication (art. Tercero, as substituted by Res. SBS 03421-2023), i.e. 12 January 2023, computed from that clause. Chapters III-VI of Title II apply gradually: Res. SBS 03421-2023 (dated 16 Oct 2023, El Peruano 19 Oct 2023) let other committees take some model-risk committee functions for lower-risk models and reset the timetable; Res. SBS 03884-2024 (dated 12 Nov 2024, El Peruano 18 Nov 2024) set the financial-system schedule: highest-risk models from 30 June 2024 (credit), 31 Dec 2024 (market/liquidity) and 31 May 2026 (operational and AML/CFT), other credit-risk models from 31 May 2025. Publication date corrected from the signing date (6 Jan 2023) to the gazette date.
instruments.summary: Binding SBS regulation requiring supervised financial, insurance and pension firms to manage the risk of models used in credit, market, liquidity, operational and AML/CFT risk management (model inventory, categorisation, governance, development standards, independent validation and monitoring). For models built with artificial-intelligence techniques it requires at least interpretability testing, hyperparameter optimisation and cross-validation or similar techniques to avoid overfitting, and validation must assess hyperparameter choices and overfitting.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Financial-sector rules with AI-specific model-risk requirements.

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 32615, Ley que establece el uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) para la protección de la vicuña y la prevención de su caza furtiva
instruments.english_title: Law No. 32615 establishing the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to protect the vicuña and prevent its poaching
instruments.issuing_authority: Congress of the Republic of Peru (law enacted by insistence and promulgated by the acting President of Congress)
instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 28 May 2026 (signed 26 May 2026 by the acting President of Congress after Congress insisted on the text approved on 6 November 2025; Congress bill 10219/2024-CR). The law has no commencement clause of its own; the Executive, through MIDAGRI, must approve its regulation within 60 calendar days of entry into force (2nd final provision). No implementing regulation found on El Peruano by 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Sector law requiring the State to use AI to protect the vicuña: MIDAGRI, through the national forestry and wildlife service SERFOR, with regional and local governments, peasant communities and the National Police, promotes AI surveillance systems (smart cameras with facial or biometric recognition of animals and people, drones and sensors) in risk zones, and centralises sensor, camera and drone data in an AI system for predictive analysis of poaching hotspots, accessible to the competent authorities. It also requires training for park rangers and communities, promotes international cooperation using AI, and amends Law 26496 on South American camelids.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI-specific sector law mandating public-sector AI surveillance and predictive analytics (including biometric recognition of people) for wildlife protection.

instruments.english_title: Peruvian Technical Standard NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system
instruments.issuing_authority: National Institute of Quality (INACAL), Dirección de Normalización (approved by Resolución Directoral N° 000013-2025-INACAL/DN)
instruments.current_status: Approved (1st edition) by Resolución Directoral N° 000013-2025-INACAL/DN dated 25 June 2025 (San Isidro), on the basis of the 16 June 2025 minutes of the Permanent Standardisation Committee, and published in El Peruano on 30 June 2025. Peruvian Technical Standards are voluntary, but DS 115-2025-PCM (art. 28.2) requires public entities to use NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 when developing AI-based systems, and the SGTD promotes it for others.
instruments.summary: National adoption, as a Peruvian Technical Standard, of ISO/IEC 42001, the international requirements standard for an AI management system (establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving AI governance in an organisation, including AI risk and impact assessment). It was approved by INACAL's Directorate of Standardisation among other NTPs under Law 30224 on the National Quality System. The AI Regulation makes its use mandatory for public-sector AI development.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National adoption of ISO/IEC 42001; mandatory for public-sector AI development under DS 115-2025-PCM.

instruments.summary: National adoption, as a Peruvian Technical Standard, of ISO/IEC 23894, the international guidance on how organisations that develop, deploy or use AI can manage AI-specific risks and integrate risk management into their AI activities. It was approved by INACAL's Directorate of Standardisation among other NTPs under Law 30224 on the National Quality System and complements NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National adoption of the ISO/IEC 23894 AI risk-management standard.

instruments.english_title: Directive No. 002-2026-PCM/SGTD establishing the profile and responsibilities of the Artificial Intelligence Officer
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Council of Ministers - Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (approved by Resolución de Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital N.° 004-2026-PCM/SGTD)
instruments.current_status: Published on the PCM page of the national government portal on 21 October 2026 (the directive's own version table says October 2026). Article 3 makes it mandatory for public administration entities, business-treatment entities and FONAFE companies; private organisations may use it as a reference. Article 11 sets maximum designation periods counted from the day after publication in El Peruano: 6 months for ministries, autonomous bodies, the judiciary, Congress, FONAFE companies and public universities; 9 months for regional governments; 12 months for type A and C municipalities. No separate commencement clause was identified.
instruments.summary: Directive of the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (the national technical-normative AI authority) setting the profile, designation criteria, duties and reporting lines of the Artificial Intelligence Officer (OIA) that public entities must appoint. It applies by entity type and sets designation deadlines of 6, 9 or 12 months, registration of the officer in the digital compliance platform, temporary assignment rules, a special regime for local governments and quarterly reporting to the entity's Digital Government and Transformation Committee. It builds on Law 31814, its Regulation (DS 115-2025-PCM) and the National AI Strategy 2026-2030.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Creates the institutional AI officer role across the Peruvian public sector under the AI Law framework.

organizations.name: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
organizations.ai_governance_role: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM). Through its Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD), it is the national technical-normative AI authority under Law 31814 (art. 4): it directs, evaluates and supervises AI use, issued the AI Law Regulation (DS 115-2025-PCM, with the refrendo of other ministers) and approved the National AI Strategy 2026-2030 (RM 152-2026-PCM); it runs the AI sandbox and the gob.pe/iaperu channel.

organizations.name: Congress of the Republic of Peru
organizations.ai_governance_role: Unicameral legislature (Congreso de la República); enacted Law 31814 promoting AI, Law 32314 adding AI to the Criminal Code and Law 29733 on personal data protection; receives the AI authority's annual report (Law 31814 art. 5); AI bills pending.

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos (MINJUSDH); its General Directorate exercises the National Authority for Personal Data Protection (ANPD), which supervises Law 29733 and its Regulation (DS 016-2024-JUS), including the right not to be subject to automated decisions; the AI Regulation refers personal-data matters in AI to it.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Peru's official gazette, the Congress bill tracker, the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, each ministry and the sector regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for procurement, readiness indices, generative AI or international agreements. Some sources were not fully checked, including the national legal database search and annexes of some ministry documents, and the government's AI ethics guidelines had not been published by 2026-10-27.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). SPIJ search, congreso.gob.pe bill-tracker search, OSIPTEL/SMV/MINSA/MININTER/SUNAT sites not reached. i-50887dc0f05b re-identified as ENIA 2026-2030 (RM 152-2026-PCM, 29 Apr 2026; El Peruano 1 May 2026). i-135a99a5a475 re-pointed to DS 115-2025-PCM; effective_date null (90 business days, no stated calendar date). i-6422ccb94106 (gob.pe orientation page summarising DS 115) dropped at merge, with its domain-named org and sources. Law 29733 dated 2011-07-03 per Congress page (text: given 2 Jul 2011). DS 016-2024-JUS read from gazette copy hosted by SMV (state body). SBS 00053-2023 amendments not reviewed. Convention 108: not a party. Thin pass 2026-10-13: 8 records re-checked. i-36a3efc5e880 (SBS 00053-2023) publication_date 2023-01-06 (signing) -> 2023-01-11 (El Peruano); effective_date 2023-01-12 computed from art. Tercero (in force the day after publication); last_amended 2024-11-18 (Res. SBS 03884-2024; also 03421-2023). Added Ley 32615 (El Peruano 2026-05-28; no commencement clause, effective_date null), NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 (RD 000013-2025-INACAL/DN, 2025-06-30), NTP-ISO/IEC 23894:2026 (RD 000019-2026-INACAL/DN, 2026-10-09), Catálogo de Aplicaciones con IA (gob.pe page date 2026-09-17; PDF undated, may be an update date). Congress bills via api.congreso.gob.pe (about 59 AI bills). Not reached: SPIJ search, DS 016-2024-JUS El Peruano supplement page, annexes of RM 903-2026/MINSA, ENGD, PNTD. Units covered: Law: El Peruano legal-norms search run for 'inteligencia artificial' back to 2023 and for standards, deepfake, automated-decision and algorithm terms: found Ley 32615 (AI for vicuña protection, 28 May 2026, recorded), INACAL RD 013-2025 and RD 019-2026 (recorded), SBS 00053-2023 amendments (record fixed), MINSA RM 903-2026 and Ley 32082/DS 015-2025-RE (leads); no deepfake or automated-decision provisions beyond Ley 32314 and the data-protection regulation. Congress bill tracker queried via its API: 50+ AI bills listed with stages; enacted ones map to Ley 31814, Ley 32314, Ley 32615 and Ley 32082; pending ones held as leads. SPIJ not queried (El Peruano search used instead).; Government: PCM/SGTD: gob.pe/iaperu, PCM norms and publications; ENIA 2026-2030, DS 115-2025-PCM and RM 132-2024-PCM re-checked; AI catalogue recorded; ENGD 2026-2030 and the 2030 Digital Transformation Policy held as leads (AI only incidental). SGTD AI ethics guidelines, AI Officer guidelines and the technology/data governance reference framework: searched on El Peruano and gob.pe, none published by 2026-10-13. No AI procurement rules found.; Ministries: Education (MINEDU): only the 2024 awareness brochure (existing lead) and AI hackathon resolutions; no AI guidance. Health (MINSA): RM 903-2026/MINSA institutional AI policy (lead). Justice (MINJUSDH): data protection law and regulation re-checked; no AI guidance. Defence (MINDEF): nothing found. Finance/tax (MEF; SUNAT): SUNAT institutional AI policy RS 000144-2026/SUNAT (lead); nothing from MEF. Labour (MTPE): only an AI job-matching platform listed in the PCM catalogue; no rules. Interior/police (MININTER/PNP): nothing found (pending video-surveillance AI bills only). Agriculture (MIDAGRI/SERFOR): designated implementer of Ley 32615 (recorded); regulation not yet published. Foreign affairs (MRE): Ley 32082 and DS 015-2025-RE on consular digital transformation incl. AI (lead). Judiciary: Lima Norte court AI tools and a CE-PJ personal-data directive only; no AI usage rules.; Regulators: SBS (banking/insurance/pensions): model-risk regulation re-checked and fixed (publication 11 Jan 2023, amendments 2023/2024); no other AI rule found. BCRP (central bank) and SMV (securities): no AI documents found (El Peruano results only staff travel). OSIPTEL (telecoms): no AI rules found. DIGEMID (medicines/devices): no AI or software-as-medical-device rules found. SUNEDU (higher education): only a 2025 draft quality regulation mentioning AI in passing. Indecopi (competition/consumer/IP): internal AI ethics guidelines only (lead). ANPD (data protection): no AI guidance or AI decisions found; directive on data protection officers and fines methodology are not AI-specific. Cyber security (National Digital Security Centre within SGTD): no separate AI security guidance. INACAL (standards): NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 and NTP-ISO/IEC 23894:2026 adoptions found and recorded; no ISO/IEC 22989 adoption found.. Not reached: SPIJ (spij.minjus.gob.pe) own search not run; El Peruano full-text search used instead; DS 016-2024-JUS special-supplement page not found in the El Peruano search (publication date still from the MINJUSDH press release); Annexes of RM 903-2026/MINSA, RM 049-2026-PCM (ENGD) and DS 085-2023-PCM (PNTD) not read; BCRP, SMV, MINDEF, MININTER and MTPE own websites not browsed individually (covered via El Peruano and web search only). Could not verify: SGTD AI ethics guidelines and AI Officer guidelines (DS 115-2025-PCM 2nd final provision; RM 152-2026-PCM): not published on El Peruano or gob.pe by 2026-10-13.; Ley 32082 own gazette text (consular digital transformation) not located; only its Regulation DS 015-2025-RE read.; Bill number of the existing lead 'Proyecto de Ley que modifica la Ley N° 31814 ... (Medina Hermosilla)' not matched to a tracker entry (candidates 13175/2025-CR, 13140/2025-CR, 13553/2025-CR; 10737/2024-CR withdrawn).; Convention 108: Peru not found as a party or invitee; no accession act found.. procurement, index-readiness, generative-ai, international: no material found.
